item.title: A cosmic 'leaf blower': Light-propelled winds help explain early universe's bright galaxies
item.description: When astronomers looked at photos of the early universe taken by the James Webb Space Telescope, they found something odd: an overabundance of bright galaxies. Based on what they knew about the early universe, such galaxies should have been far less common in the few hundred million years following the Big Bang.

item.title: A tiny shift exposes a cold brown dwarf masquerading as an early galaxy
item.description: A faint red object spotted by the James Webb Space Telescope originally appeared to offer a possible glimpse of the universe's first galaxies. But images taken about 3½ years apart revealed a giveaway: The object, nicknamed Capotauro, had moved.

item.title: The telescope that could reveal what dark matter and dark energy are
item.description: The Roman telescope is NASA’s newest space observatory. Every 10 months, it will get the equivalent of about 1000 years' worth of Hubble observations. Will it find the answers to our questions about dark matter and dark energy?
